Known-good QA fixture

Objectives
  • Complete a safe interaction and explain why it is safe.
  1. Activity 1
  2. Activity 2
  3. Activity 3

Teaching

Direct controls work without network access. Complete work stays in place when you revisit an activity.

Another way to think about it Optional example

Imagine a shopper walking one aisle, placing only the useful items into a fresh basket.

A comprehension similarly gathers chosen items into a new collection during one pass.

Where this fits

Decision: Decide whether the effect should stay on this page or cross a boundary.

Good fit: Use the local control for a small, self-contained practice change.

Choose something else when: The work must contact another system or coordinate several dependent steps.

Activity 1 — Your task: choose a safe action

Choose the safe action, then compare it with the explained result.

Need a hint?

Where to act: Look at the safe-action controls below your note.

Next step: Rule out any action that sends information elsewhere.

Need a hint?

Where to act: Compare the two result buttons below your note.

Next step: Prefer the action whose effect stays inside this page.

What success looks like

Your note remains when you leave and return, and the local result is explained.

0 of 1

Challenge (optional)

Optional time: about 2 minutes

Success criteria: Write two safe actions using only the controls already taught.

Activity 2 — Your task: explain your choice

Explain why your first action stays local.

Activity checks

Your explanation names the boundary that keeps the action safe.

Back to activity 1

Activity 3 — Your task: recap

Review your saved note and explanation.

What success looks like

You can state which action is safe and why.

Back to activity 2

Recap

Use direct controls and check resulting state.
